trace.title: Record key
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

A Kafka topic is split into partitions. Each partition is an ordered append log with offsets.

Offset 10 in partition 0 is unrelated to offset 10 in partition 1; it is not a global event number.

A record key helps the partitioner place related records together under a stable configuration. Using ticket identity as the key can keep that ticket’s records on one partition.

It does not order all tickets globally. A single very hot key can limit useful parallelism.

Adding partitions can change key-to-partition mapping. If per-entity ordering matters across such a change, plan migration/transition semantics rather than assuming the old placement stays unchanged.

Also keep application version/sequence checks when events can be retried or produced through several paths.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Producer chooses key → partitioner selects partition → leader appends record → offset identifies its position → assigned consumer processes that partition. Two partitions can advance at different speeds.

Draw A1/A2 in one partition and B1/B2 in another. There is no single cross-partition order you can infer merely from their offsets.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
A key is not a global lock. A large number of partitions is not free operationally.

Changing keys can scatter one entity’s history.
